_comment: Last-mile delivery scenario. THERE IS NO ROAD NETWORK IN THIS MODEL - every route is cross-country. That makes it wrong for ordinary logistics and right for the case it is built for: roads cut, bridges down, and a hub that can no longer reach the settlements it serves by the usual means.
_demandNote: demandKg is what each settlement needs delivered in one cycle. Populations and demands here are illustrative, not survey data.
_scaleNote: Settlements sit 4 to 11 km from the hub, which is what last-mile actually means. An earlier version placed them 12 to 30 km out and every platform failed on endurance: correct arithmetic, useless plan. If real settlements are that far out, the finding is that the hub is in the wrong place.
